Frecce Tricolori’s M-346PAN Officially Unveiled

Published on: November 26, 2026 at 7:38 PM CET Follow Us On Google News
Stefano D'Urso
The M-346 PAN takes off for the demonstration at the start of the official roll out ceremony. (Image credit: Lorenzo Giacobbo)
SHARE

The M-346 in PAN configuration for the Italian Air Force’s Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team has been officially unveiled at Leonardo’s Venegono plant.

Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:56
Instaread

Leonardo and the Italian Air Force have officially unveiled the new M-346 in the PAN configuration (from Pattuglia Acrobatica Nazionale – National Aerobatic Team) that will equip the Frecce Tricolori. Although it has been flying for a month, the aircraft was presented during a ceremony at Leonardo’s Venegono plant on Nov. 26, 2026.

Our friend and contributor Lorenzo Giacobbo was in Venegono and captured the aircraft on camera as it performed over the airfield at the ceremony.

The event saw the participation of Leonardo’s CEO Lorenzo Mariani, the Italian Air Force’s Chief of Staff, Lt Gen Antonio Conserva, and the Frecce Tricolori’s new commander, Lt Col Pierluigi Raspa. Raspa took command of the aerobatic team on Nov. 18, and during his assignment will also oversee the transition from the MB-339PAN to the M-346.

“It is a truly moving experience to see this remarkable achievement of Italian technology take to the skies,” said Lt Gen Conserva. “The transition from the illustrious MB-339 to the M-346 marks another step forward, embracing the challenges of the future while remaining true to the values that have always defined the Frecce Tricolori. The Italian flag that we will continue to fly in skies around the world symbolises our national unity, the professionalism of the men and women of the Italian Air Force and the wider defence community, as well as our country’s ingenuity, creativity, and technological and industrial excellence.”

Before the ceremony, guests were welcomed in the final assembly facility, where six more aircraft are already in various stages of manufacturing. The M-346s are expected to be delivered throughout 2027, to allow the team to start training on the new aircraft after the final airshow season with the MB-339PAN.

Earlier this week, the M-346PAN rehearsed a flight demo with Commander Giacomo “Jack” Iannelli, Head of Trainers Project Test Pilot at Leonardo, at the controls, showing the jet’s agility, and included Schneider turns, inverted flight, loopings, tonneauxs and a Cuban eight. This demo was then flown again by Iannelli at the start of the Nov. 26 ceremony, with the aircraft now featuring the complete livery with the addition of the Frecce Tricolori markings on the tail and the ‘0’ number of the team’s commander.

Leonardo says that “activities are proceeding on schedule and as planned, with the training of pilots and technicians, close collaboration between industry and the Italian Air Force, and the development of a renewed aerobatic flight programme that will benefit from the new aircraft’s distinctive and advanced capabilities.” The company added that the program also includes a comprehensive technical and logistics support package, training and simulation systems for pilots and maintenance personnel, as well as infrastructure upgrades at Rivolto Air Base, home to the 313th Aerobatic Training Squadron Frecce Tricolori.

M-346PAN

As we previously reported, the M-346 Advanced Jet Trainer (T-346A in accordance with the Italian MOD Mission Design Series) was chosen as the successor of the Frecce Tricolori’s MB-339s in 2024. The decision was announced during an event celebrating the team’s return from their North America Tour 2024.

The Frecce Tricolori would get 15 M-346s: ten for their main formation, plus the one of the commander and four spares. These aircraft will be in the same configuration of the ones already in service with the Italian Air Force, but with some additional customized features.

The first is the smoke system, which consists of a ventral tank that acts as a reservoir for the smoke fluids and two smoke lines installed in the fuselage. Leonardo says the tank is divided into three sections, one for each of the three colors of the Italian flag – green, white and red.

The pilot has two controls, one on the control stick and one on the throttle, to control the smoke’s release. A control panel in the cockpit allows the tanks and smoke controls to be linked.

As on the MB-339PANs, the white smoke consists of vaseline oil, while the red and green are obtained by mixing the vaseline oil with specific pigments. The liquids are injected through two nozzles at the end of the engine exhaust, where they vaporize due to the high temperature.

A second feature is the addition of a dedicated system to enable the live transmission of footage captured by on-board cameras, to support the Frecce Tricolori’s operational, training and multimedia requirements. The aircraft will be fitted with eight cameras installed at various points on the fuselage, which will transmit images in real time via a dedicated data link to the event’s video control center.

Leonardo said that no significant modifications have been made to the aircraft’s general systems, but some specific modifications are planned to support the requirements of aerobatic flight. Among these is the information provided by the Head-Up Display and audio system, as sets of distinctive symbols have been introduced on the aircraft’s various visual and audio systems, and the positioning of certain controls has been adjusted.

Additionally, an ‘Acro Mode’ allows to reduce pilot’s workload during formation flight. The Acro Mode specifically controls the movement of the airbrake, distinguishing it from the movement in normal flight mode, and thus, when the control is pressed, the airbrake is either fully extended or fully retracted.

Finally, the M-346PAN includes a retractable ladder stowed in a compartment in the forward fuselage to allow the pilot to board and disembark from the aircraft. The ladder is extended manually by ground crew and secured to the canopy spar to allow the pilot to use it.

The Aviationist understands that the M-346’s wings have also been reinforced to resists to the stressed of aerobatic flight. The aircraft has also been lightened and flight control software received some modifications, allowing to push the flight envelope.

A new livery

As we reported on occasion of the rollout, the aircraft has been painted in the new livery announced in 2024, although it is still missing the number and the Frecce Tricolori markings on the tail. The new livery is designed by Pininfarina, the renowned Italian design and engineering firm famous for its work in the automotive industry, particularly in the design of luxury and high-performance vehicles.

However, the new livery has been met by criticism by many aviation enthusiasts before of the many differences when compared with the current livery. In fact, this livery is characterized by a matte dark blue, instead of the glossy blue associated with the Frecce’s MB-339s.

Additionally, a large white patch covers the dorsal area of the M-346, while a white line can be seen on the underside. This line will accompanied by the green and the red on separate sides to make up for the Italian flag’s colors, replacing the symmetric design used on the MB-339.

When the livery was unveiled in 2024, statements mentioned it has been designed to highlight the Frecce Tricolori’s flight through a three-dimensional design, ensuring that there is always a recognizable graphic element capable of conveying a sense of speed and dynamism to the audience during the maneuvers. However, in addition to these aesthetic reasons, there are also functional reasons.

Starting from the main color, the most criticized aspect, the darker, matte blue and the large use of white increase the M-346’s visual contrast against the clear sky and in overcast sky, respectively. Additionally, the asymmetry obtained on the underside with the green on the right side, the white in the middle and the red on the left allows the pilots to immediately identify the orientation and positioning of the aircraft during formation flight and maneuvers.
